D001.screening_reason: Main outcome is academic performance (GPA); insomnia and stress are predictors
D001.summary_en: Models the link between insomnia and academic performance in 996 undergraduates using questionnaire data, clustering and supervised classifiers. Classifiers reach AUC 0.96; sleep-onset difficulty, perceived stress and caffeine are the dominant predictors of academic decline.

D002.summary_en: Identifies predictors of music performance anxiety in 599 Chinese music students with four ML models, SHAP, latent profile and mediation analysis. Random forest performs best; emotion-oriented coping, perceived stress, maladaptive perfectionism, self-efficacy and social support are the main predictors.

D003.summary_en: Builds ML models that predict students' physical and emotional well-being in classrooms from IoT indoor/outdoor environmental data, infrastructure status and student surveys over five months. The tool supports proactive classroom environment management.

D004.screening_reason: Population not described as students (public wearable datasets)
D004.summary_en: Compares feature-based ML and deep learning for stress detection from smartwatch signals across four public datasets. DL performs better within datasets but loses about 21% F1 across datasets; transfer learning reduces the gap.

D005.screening_reason: Alzheimer's disease imaging; not students or mental health analytics
D005.summary_en: Compares tau-PET spatial extent and tau load as predictors of brain hypometabolism and cognition in Alzheimer's disease.

D006.screening_reason: Population-level suicide rates in Brazil; not students
D006.summary_en: Analyses municipal suicide rates in Brazil (2009-2023) with XGBoost and healthcare infrastructure data; mental health facilities correlate with lower suicide rates.

D007.summary_en: Examines how health literacy relates to life satisfaction via exercise adherence and rest intolerance in 21,095 students from 104 Chinese universities, combining mediation analysis and ML with SHAP. Exercise adherence, health literacy and rest intolerance are the key predictors.

D008.screening_reason: Glaucoma progression; not students or mental health
D008.summary_en: Develops a deep learning model that predicts glaucoma progression from fundus photographs.

D009.summary_en: Detects depression from acoustic and linguistic speech features in 151 Spanish-speaking clinical participants. The linguistic model outperforms the acoustic model (AUC 0.86 vs 0.79).

D010.summary_en: Extracts interpretable decision-tree patterns from three student mental health datasets. Coping difficulty is the most informative predictor of stress and nervousness, followed by anger over poor performance and difficulty relaxing.

D011.summary_en: Develops a probability-strength stacking ensemble for depression risk on a Kaggle dataset of 27,901 college students. It reaches AUC 0.919, similar to CatBoost; SHAP identifies suicidal ideation, academic pressure and financial stress as top predictors.

D012.screening_reason: Mixed cohorts; students are one of three groups
D012.summary_en: Evaluates a domain-adaptive neural uplift model across medical students, quarantined adults and psychiatric patients (n = 2,624). Adaptation gives modest, tuning-sensitive gains.

D013.screening_reason: Public satisfaction with climate policy; not students' mental health
D013.summary_en: Analyses determinants of public satisfaction with government climate actions in China.

D014.summary_en: Classifies youth aged 8-16 with specific learning disorders (70) versus peers (130) from cognitive and socio-emotional variables with SVM. Test anxiety, social anxiety, loneliness and maladaptive emotion regulation characterise the disorder group.

D015.summary_en: Forecasts medical waste generation in hospitals with ML and Monte Carlo simulation.

D016.summary_en: Identifies internet addiction risk in 1,177 vocational college students with three ML models, SHAP and latent profile analysis. Emotional exhaustion, anxiety, depression and stress are the strongest predictors; a high-distress, high-self-esteem subgroup is especially vulnerable.

D017.summary_en: Randomised trial of pharmacy incentives for long-acting contraception in Kenya.

D018.summary_en: Analyses 25,219 evaluation texts on supervisor-graduate student relationships from 445 Chinese universities with BERT-based sentiment analysis and topic modelling, proposing a four-type typology and an early warning tool to protect student well-being.

D019.summary_en: Detects severe depression in students with tuned ML and ensemble classifiers; AdaBoost reaches 77.2% accuracy.

D020.summary_en: Uses the Norwegian SHoT2018 student survey (34,469 participants) to model chronic pain, psychological distress and their co-occurrence with three classifiers and SHAP, validated across regions. Female sex, perceived health and sleep disorders relate to all conditions.

D021.summary_en: Predicts psychological resilience in 360 university students from diet, smoking, alcohol and body image with random forest and TabNet. Accuracy is moderate; perceived health and body image are the key predictors.

D022.screening_reason: Children's school travel and social outcomes; not mental health analytics
D022.summary_en: Uses a Bayesian belief network on 601 primary school children to relate school travel to social contact, cohesion and perceived safety.

D023.summary_en: Presents ANXIETY-CARE, an anxiety detection system based on sweat (electrodermal) sensors with XGBoost and CNN/LSTM models. The LSTM reaches 84.3% accuracy on the StudentLife dataset.

D024.screening_reason: Active school transportation prevalence; not mental health
D024.summary_en: Predicts child active school transportation prevalence from built-environment data with ML.

D025.screening_reason: School building energy and thermal comfort simulation; no student data
D025.summary_en: Optimises school building design for energy use and thermal comfort in Iran with simulated scenarios and gradient boosting.

D026.screening_reason: General adult population prevalence study; no analytics on students
D026.summary_en: Estimates the prevalence of DSM-5 disorders in a representative sample of Hong Kong adults.

D027.summary_en: Proposes a multimodal framework (physiological signals, self-reports and surveys), refined with a Delphi process, to assess stress and well-being of cognitively strong students using LLM sentiment analysis and classical ML.

D028.summary_en: Predicts loneliness at school in 60,498 students aged 10 and 15 (SSES survey) with elastic net, random forest, XGBoost and XAI. Bullying is the strongest predictor; extraversion and emotional stability are protective.

D029.screening_reason: Cognitive health of middle-aged and older adults
D029.summary_en: Estimates the effect of high-speed rail on cognitive health of older Chinese adults with double machine learning.

D030.screening_reason: Postpartum depression in mothers; not students
D030.summary_en: Identifies postpartum depression subtypes in a Norwegian cohort of women with unsupervised clustering.

D031.summary_en: Predicts session-by-session psychotherapy outcomes for CBT outpatients with mixed-model trees.

D032.summary_en: Examines how technology dependence relates to oral English anxiety in 716 Chinese university students, combining structural equation modelling with XGBoost-SHAP. Psychological burden amplifies the association and digital self-efficacy buffers it; neuroticism increases vulnerability.

D033.screening_reason: Alzheimer's disease trajectories in patients; not students
D033.summary_en: Identifies diagnostic trajectories leading to Alzheimer's disease from electronic health records.

D034.screening_reason: Outcome is perceived environmental dissatisfaction linked to well-being
D034.summary_en: Predicts students' perceived dissatisfaction with indoor environmental quality in a Norwegian school from sensor data, weather, building parameters and 1,437 survey responses. Random forest performs best; SHAP highlights CO2, VOCs, humidity and temperature.

D035.summary_en: Proposes single-case learning analytics combining quantitative and qualitative longitudinal data to assess well-being support in doctoral workshops (105 doctoral students), showing who benefits more or less.

D036.screening_reason: Outcome is general self-efficacy, not a mental health or well-being measure
D036.summary_en: Predicts general self-efficacy of 612,004 students aged 15-16 from 79 countries (PISA 2018) with Lasso and XGBoost. Mastery goal orientation, meaning of life and positive emotions are the top predictors.

D037.summary_en: Develops a computerised adaptive test of mental well-being for undergraduates in South Africa and Nigeria, calibrating 375 items with a graded IRT model to a 175-item adaptive scale.

D038.summary_en: Presents MindLift, a multimodal platform (behaviour, voice tone, facial expression, text sentiment) using CNN, RNN and transformer models with a CBT-based chatbot. Reports increased engagement but no specific metrics.

D039.summary_en: Qualitative interviews with 21 first-year university students and three instructors on how generative AI affects emotional engagement and well-being in language learning; GenAI is perceived to reduce anxiety and stress.

D040.screening_reason: Outcome is team participation quality (relational well-being)
D040.summary_en: Evaluates an AI team-composition algorithm for challenge-based learning, using relational well-being as a measure of participation quality.

D041.summary_en: Post-hoc analysis of clinical decision rules for antibiotic duration in bloodstream infection.

D042.screening_reason: Outcome is situational engagement, not mental health
D042.summary_en: Examines situational engagement in online climate education courses with ecological momentary assessment and two-level regression.

D043.summary_en: Predicts severe newborn acidemia from computerised cardiotocography and clinical features.

D044.summary_en: Uses random forest regression, neural networks and SEM on 524 undergraduates to relate mindfulness, psychological flexibility and rumination to mental health and well-being. Psychological flexibility and rumination mediate the effect of mindfulness.

D045.summary_en: Detects depression in Bangladeshi university students with ML, deep learning and language models, handling imbalance with resampling. Random forest reaches 91.1% accuracy and RoBERTa 98.6% recall; SHAP and LIME explain predictions.

D046.summary_en: Identifies newborn auricular deformities from smartphone photos with deep learning.

D047.summary_en: Predicts post-discharge falls in older adults with ML classifiers.

D048.summary_en: Predicts depression in 750 Bangladeshi university students with a survey designed with psychologists and seven ML models. Random forest performs best (87% accuracy, 95% recall).

D049.screening_reason: Neuroimaging data repository for psychiatry; not students (abstract truncated)
D049.summary_en: Describes a multi-site neuroimaging data repository for psychiatric machine learning research (abstract truncated in the source).

D050.screening_reason: Outcome is attention during an assessment, not mental health
D050.summary_en: Classifies students' attention during a programming assessment from eye-tracking features with ML and deep learning models.

D051.screening_reason: Teachers, qualitative; not students or analytics
D051.summary_en: Qualitative interview study on immunity and vision of Iranian EFL teachers.

D052.screening_reason: Student profiling; well-being is a secondary implication
D052.summary_en: Clusters 30,800 Spanish 15-year-old students (PISA 2022) with explainable ML; socio-economic status and ICT access differentiate seven profiles.

D053.summary_en: Simplifies the University Personality Inventory with ML using 5,155 college students. Random forest reaches 89.4% accuracy while reducing the scale from 60 to 6 items.

D054.summary_en: Screens depression with the GHQ-12 and socio-demographic items in 804 Bangladeshi university students using 16 ML models; about 60% show depression and Extra Trees performs best (90.26%).

D055.screening_reason: Physical function of badminton players; not mental health
D055.summary_en: Evaluates college badminton players' physical function with a PSO-BP neural network.

D056.screening_reason: Outcome is heavy drinking onset; mental health metrics are predictors
D056.summary_en: Forecasts heavy drinking onset after high school from mental health metrics in 559 young adults (NCANDA) followed for 8 years; risk factors differ by pathway and sex.

D057.screening_reason: Thermal comfort modelling in schools; not mental health analytics
D057.summary_en: Improves thermal sensation prediction models for students in naturally ventilated Mediterranean schools.

D058.screening_reason: Clinical decision support for depression in patients; not students
D058.summary_en: Case study and recommendations for implementing an AI clinical decision support system for major depressive disorder.

D059.summary_en: Predicts ureteroscopic laser lithotripsy outcomes with ML ensembles.

D060.summary_en: Calibrates low-cost NO2 sensors with a neural network.

D061.summary_en: Forecasts college students' positive and negative affect one week ahead by combining wearable sensor data with self-reported diaries in a transformer plus language model, from a one-year longitudinal study. Accuracy is about 82.5%.

D062.screening_reason: Thermal sensation prediction in classrooms; not mental health
D062.summary_en: Predicts university students' thermal sensation in naturally ventilated classrooms with ANN and random forest models.

D063.summary_en: Identifies factors of mobile phone addiction in 3,000 college students in Zhejiang with ML; perfectionism is the main factor and the prediction model reaches 76.68% accuracy.

D064.summary_en: Diagnoses social anxiety disorder from demographic, emotional and physical symptoms with several ML models and four XAI techniques. AdaBoost and logistic regression reach 88%; the Liebowitz scale and fear of public speaking are the key attributes.

D065.screening_reason: Clinical EEG depression detection; not students
D065.summary_en: Detects depression from EEG signals of clinical patients with a deep wavelet scattering network.

D066.screening_reason: AI in education for sustainable development; not mental health
D066.summary_en: Critical review of AI tools such as ChatGPT in education for sustainable development.

D067.summary_en: Builds an intelligent mental health assessment system for college students with big data mining algorithms, reporting 95-97% accuracy without describing the data.

D068.summary_en: Proposes a data mining model (PCA, discriminant analysis and regression) to evaluate students' mental health status; no metrics are reported.

D069.summary_en: Combines unsupervised and supervised ML on university students using a mental health app across three COVID-19 timepoints. Three subgroups emerge; the situational well-being group is sensitive to stressors and shows burnout.

D070.summary_en: Proposes a post-disaster diagnostic model that uses sentiment analysis and an ensemble classifier to grade students' depression and anxiety and schedule therapy. It detects 44% of cases versus 7-15% with conventional monitoring.

D071.screening_reason: Indoor air quality and thermal comfort in schools; no student mental health data
D071.summary_en: Predicts indoor air quality and thermal comfort levels in naturally ventilated schools with a class-weighted random forest.

D072.screening_reason: Tunisian general population; students are only one subgroup
D072.summary_en: Mines association rules for factors linked to psychiatric disorders in the Tunisian population during COVID-19.

D073.summary_en: Develops AIDA, a hybrid depression scale built from eight existing scales and applied to 520 Bangladeshi students, with ten ML and two deep learning models. Random forest reaches 98.08% accuracy; LIME explains predictions.

D074.summary_en: Predicts perceived psychological and social stress in 444 university students during COVID-19 with supervised ML, PCA and hyperparameter optimisation. About 24% show extremely high psychological stress; the MLP reaches 80.5% accuracy.

D075.screening_reason: Patients with severe mental illness; medical students used only as an application sample
D075.summary_en: Detects severe mental illness from clinical MRI with a multiple-instance deep learning model (AUC 0.82) and tests it on 148 medical students, where it predicts clinician-rated distress better than self-reports.

D076.summary_en: Compares tourism safety topics in Web of Science and Weibo posts.

D077.summary_en: Predicts depression in 284 engineering students at a Peruvian public university with stacking ensembles and oversampling; the best stacking model reaches 94.69% accuracy.

D078.screening_reason: Healthcare analytics capacity in hospitals; off-topic
D078.summary_en: Surveys analytics awareness and skills in an Irish hospital group.

D079.summary_en: Applies association rules and clustering to junior school students' pubertal timing and social adaptability scale data, as part of adolescent mental health education.

D080.summary_en: Predicts university students' subjective well-being from wearable step count, heart rate and sleep data (NetHealth, University of Notre Dame) with several classifiers; accuracy is 62%.

D081.screening_reason: Outcome is dropout; mental well-being is one predictor
D081.summary_en: Predicts dropout of 91 engineering students in Brazil with a C4.5 decision tree (86.81%); interaction with professors, curriculum and mental well-being are key factors.

D082.summary_en: Classifies anxiety levels of 127 Indian engineering students from a Likert questionnaire with four ML algorithms; random forest reaches 78.9%.

D083.summary_en: Analyses viewer data of an informal science animation channel on YouTube.

D084.summary_en: Predicts COVID-19 burnout in Indian healthcare workers from ECG heart rate variability with ML.

D085.summary_en: Systematic review of predictive models for total knee arthroplasty outcomes.

D086.summary_en: Develops a dynamic model predicting psychological treatment outcomes for NHS patients from session-by-session symptom data.
